perf-canary-bot: :rotating_light: fast tier p99 regression detected (blocker candidate)
- Suite: `mixed_workload_slo_tiers`
- Model family: `qwen2.5-32b-instruct`
- Hardware: `h100-80gb`
- Region: `us-east-1`
- Metric: `latency_ms_p99`
- Baseline: 1180ms  ->  Current: 1715ms (+45%)
- Build: `runtime@1.22.0-rc3` (commit 9d3a1c8)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.inference/d/perf-canary/fast-tier?var-model=qwen2.5-32b-instruct&var-region=us-east-1

Marcus Reed: seeing the same locally from perf suite. p50/p95 basically unchanged, but p99 blows out on the mixed prompt-length case (short+long prompts, 35% streaming). only qwen2.5-32b seems affected. llama3.1-70b + mixtral look fine.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, let’s treat as scheduler/regression until proven otherwise. did this start after PR-28458 or after the streaming/length bucket wiring (PR-28445)?

Marcus Reed: bisect says starts at `pr-28458` (fast-tier admission + wait budget). doesn’t repro if I flip `scheduler.fast_tier.admission_control=false`.

Omar El-Sayed: that matches the symptom: p99 only, suggests we’re occasionally holding a request too long behind prefill batches.

Julian Moore: any queue stats? want to see if it’s actual overload or self-inflicted waiting.

Marcus Reed: pulled a trace snippet from the canary run. looks like “fast tier max wait” triggers, then we requeue and it loops.

Marcus Reed: logs (redacted ids):
```text
[fast-tier] req=8f3c... stream=true prompt_tokens=146 decode_tokens=256
  enqueue_ts=... queue_depth=7
  decision: admit=false reason=WAIT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED wait_ms=24 max_wait_ms=20
  action: requeue priority=normal

[fast-tier] req=8f3c... (same)
  enqueue_ts=... queue_depth=6
  decision: admit=false reason=PREFILL_BATCH_LOCKED prefill_inflight=1
  action: requeue priority=normal

[fast-tier] req=8f3c...
  enqueue_ts=... queue_depth=10
  decision: admit=true batch_tokens=6144 batch_reqs=11
  latency_total_ms=1822 prefill_ms=410 decode_ms=1204 queue_wait_ms=185
```

Sofia Ivanova: that first line is suspicious: `wait_ms=24 max_wait_ms=20` but why did it sit to 24? are we checking wait budget only when we get the scheduler tick, not continuously?

Noah Patel: yep, we only evaluate on tick / batch formation. so you can exceed by (tick interval + mutex contention). but +4ms shouldn’t cause +500ms p99 unless we’re creating a “requeue storm”.

Julian Moore: requeue storms + priority inversion are my fear. we requeue at normal priority, so a request that barely misses the fast wait budget can get stuck behind long prefills again.

Omar El-Sayed: and qwen2.5-32b might be more prefill-heavy relative to decode, so prefill mutex time dominates. if we serialize prefill more than expected, tail gets worse.

Rina Kobayashi: from benchmark-lab runs last week, qwen2.5-32b has spikier prefill when prompt_tokens > ~2k. mixed workload has 10% 2k-4k prompts. could be enough.

Marcus Reed: adding more data. queue depth isn’t huge (avg 3-5), but we see periodic prefill batches hitting `max_batch_prefill_tokens` and holding the prefill lane for ~350-450ms.

grafana-bot: Panel snapshot requested by Marcus Reed
https://grafana.redwood.inference/render/d-solo/perf-canary/fast-tier?panelId=42&var-model=qwen2.5-32b-instruct&var-region=us-east-1

Sean Gallagher: from SRE angle: if this is a real fast-tier p99 regression, we can’t roll forward without mitigation. do we have a safe knob to tighten prefill batching for fast tier only?

Sofia Ivanova: fast tier is supposed to protect tail via smaller waits, but if the prefill lane is monopolized by long prompts we need a starvation guard.

Noah Patel: hypothesis: PR-28458 introduced a single wait budget across both prefill+decode admission, but we didn’t add “short request bypass” when prefill lane is saturated.

Julian Moore: also, the reason code `PREFILL_BATCH_LOCKED` means we’re respecting a prefill batch lock to avoid thrash. that’s good, but for fast tier we might want a second lane or preempt.

Omar El-Sayed: preempting prefill batch formation is hard. but we can change the batch builder to cap prefill batch *duration* indirectly: cap prefill tokens when there are fast-tier streaming requests waiting.

Marcus Reed: what if we add a rule:
- if `tier=fast` AND `streaming=true` AND `queue_wait_ms > X` then reduce prefill batch target tokens (or force batch cut) for that tick.

Sofia Ivanova: yes, something like “cut batch early when fast-tier deadline approaching”. we already compute `oldest_wait_ms`.

Noah Patel: careful: we don’t want to tank throughput by always cutting. only when we detect mixed workload + long prompts.

Rina Kobayashi: can we use prompt length bucket as a proxy? eg when `p_prompt_len_bucket=long` is present, don’t let it join prefill batch in fast tier if there’s any short/streaming waiting.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. simplest anti-starvation: split queue into two buckets for fast tier prefill selection: short-first. long prompts can still run, but not at expense of many short ones.

Julian Moore: we already have length buckets wired in pr-28445. but pr-28458 probably didn’t use them in the admission path.

Marcus Reed: confirm: selection currently is FIFO within fast tier queue (stable by arrival). so one long prompt at head can keep getting picked into prefill batches.

Sofia Ivanova: ok proposed tweak:
1) For fast tier batch formation: pick from queue with a bias: `short_prompt_bucket` first (and/or streaming first), up to N reqs or M tokens.
2) Add a cap: if `oldest_wait_ms > 0.75*max_wait_ms`, cut prefill batch early (don’t chase target tokens).
3) When we requeue due to `WAIT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, bump priority within fast tier (anti-loop).

Noah Patel: (2) is low-risk and should directly help p99. (1) is bigger behavioral change but likely correct for fast tier semantics.

Sean Gallagher: (2) + (3) sounds like a minimal patch to unblock rollout. (1) can follow if still bad.

Omar El-Sayed: agree. requeue loop is the killer. if we miss the wait budget once, we shouldn’t get stuck behind another long prefill batch.

Julian Moore: I can implement (3) as “requeue with `priority=fast_deadline`” and treat it as a separate deque drained before normal fast-tier.

Marcus Reed: I’ll add a perf-suite scenario to specifically catch this (fast tier + streaming + long-prompt interleave) so it doesn’t regress again.

Sofia Ivanova: action items:
- Julian: patch scheduler requeue priority for fast tier on `WAIT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` + `PREFILL_BATCH_LOCKED` combos? (start with wait budget)
- Omar: add the “cut batch early when oldest_wait nearing deadline” guard in prefill batch builder
- Marcus/Rina: rerun qwen2.5-32b mixed workload on h100 and a10, confirm p99 back within gate

Noah Patel: before we touch anything, quick sanity: is qwen2.5-32b running a different kv-cache block size or anything that would cause prefill lock longer?

Marcus Reed: checked model metadata; same kernel path as before, only scheduler changed. kv-cache utilization looks fine. regression aligns exactly with PR-28458.

Omar El-Sayed: here’s a code pointer: `BatchBuilder::fill_prefill_batch()` currently keeps adding until `target_prefill_tokens` even if oldest request is about to violate wait. we can short-circuit when `deadline_ms - now_ms < tick_ms`.

Julian Moore: I’ll open a draft PR in ~1h. naming: `fast-tier: deadline-aware requeue priority`.

Sean Gallagher: pls include a temporary flag so SRE can flip if it surprises us in canary. (feature flag or config knob).

Sofia Ivanova: +1. gate it under `scheduler.fast_tier.deadline_requeue_boost=true` default on for canary only.

Marcus Reed: posting a small excerpt from perf run w/ local hack (I manually forced “cut batch early” when oldest_wait>15ms). p99 drops from ~1.7s to ~1.2s and throughput only -3% on qwen mix. seems promising.

Rina Kobayashi: that’s within noise. good.

Noah Patel: ok, sounds like correct direction. but verify no starvation of long prompts (we can accept higher long-prompt latency, but not infinite).

Omar El-Sayed: we’ll keep fairness: only cut early when oldest_wait close to deadline; otherwise normal fill.

Julian Moore: draft PR plan:
- Add `fast_deadline_queue` (bounded) for requeued requests that exceeded wait.
- Drain `fast_deadline_queue` first each tick.
- Emit reason code `REQUEUE_DEADLINE_BOOST` to observe.

Sofia Ivanova: great. please also add a counter metric: `scheduler_fast_requeue_boost_total{model,tier,region}` sampled.

Sean Gallagher: and add to dashboard for canary watch.

Marcus Reed: I’ll update perf-canary notes: if patch lands, we rerun baseline for qwen2.5-32b and watch p99 and `queue_wait_ms` distribution. will post results.

perf-canary-bot: Reminder: regression gate will remain failing until a new baseline is approved OR metric returns within threshold.

Sofia Ivanova: ack. we’re not refreshing baselines for this; must actually fix.

Omar El-Sayed: pushing branch now with early-cut guard. will ping when CI green.

Julian Moore: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/pr-28497-fast-tier-deadline-requeue-boost (draft)

Marcus Reed: :eyes: will pull and test.

Sean Gallagher: thanks all. please loop me once we have canary numbers; if still shaky we’ll keep the kill switch off for fast tier in hosted subset.

Sofia Ivanova: last note: if qwen still weird after this, we may need the bigger change (length-bucket bias), but let’s try minimal first.
